title: Scoparone inhibits the progression of gastric cancer by regulating the PIN1/STING/TBK1/IRF3 signaling pathway.
one_liner_zh: 该文研究Scoparone通过PIN1/STING/TBK1/IRF3信号通路抑制胃癌进展，仅涉及小分子-蛋白对接，无蛋白质-DNA互作体系、结合建模或AI/物理模拟方法，与本课题无关。
abstract: Gastric cancer (GC) remains a prevalent malignancy with poor outcomes in advanced stages. This study investigated the anti-GC effect of Scoparone (SCO) and elucidated its underlying mechanism involving the PIN1/STING/TBK1/IRF3 signaling pathway. GC cell lines (AGS and HGC-27) were treated with increasing concentrations of SCO, and subsequent assessments of proliferation, migration, and invasion were performed using colony formation, EdU, wound healing, and Transwell assays. Mechanistically, molecular docking was performed to predict the binding between SCO and PIN1. and Western blot analysis was further employed to evaluate the phosphorylation levels of key proteins in the PIN1/STING/TBK1/IRF3 axis. While stable knockdown and overexpression models were established in vitro to validate the pivotal role of PIN1, a subcutaneous xenograft model in nude mice was utilized to independently assess the in vivo antitumor efficacy of SCO. Our results demonstrated that SCO concentration-dependently inhibited GC cell proliferation, migration, and invasion. Mechanistically, SCO downregulated PIN1 expression and promoted the phosphorylation of STING, TBK1, and IRF3. Notably, PIN1 knockdown recapitulated and enhanced SCO-mediated suppression of malignant phenotypes as well as activation of the STING/TBK1/IRF3 pathway, whereas PIN1 overexpression partially reversed these effects. In vivo, SCO significantly suppressed tumor growth through regulation of the PIN1/STING/TBK1/IRF3 pathway. Collectively, these findings elucidate a novel mechanism by which SCO suppresses GC progression via the PIN1/STING/TBK1/IRF3 axis, providing a preclinical rationale for developing SCO as a promising therapeutic candidate for GC.
abstract_zh: 胃癌（GC）仍是一种常见的恶性肿瘤，晚期预后较差。本研究探讨了滨蒿内酯（SCO）的抗胃癌作用，并阐明了其涉及PIN1/STING/TBK1/IRF3信号通路的潜在机制。用递增浓度的SCO处理胃癌细胞系（AGS和HGC-27），随后通过集落形成、EdU、伤口愈合和Transwell实验评估增殖、迁移和侵袭能力。在机制层面，采用分子对接预测SCO与PIN1之间的结合，并进一步使用Western blot分析评估PIN1/STING/TBK1/IRF3轴中关键蛋白的磷酸化水平。在体外建立稳定敲低和过表达模型以验证PIN1的关键作用，同时利用裸鼠皮下异种移植模型独立评估SCO的体内抗肿瘤疗效。结果表明，SCO浓度依赖性地抑制胃癌细胞增殖、迁移和侵袭。在机制上，SCO下调PIN1表达并促进STING、TBK1和IRF3的磷酸化。值得注意的是，PIN1敲低重现并增强了SCO介导的恶性表型抑制以及STING/TBK1/IRF3通路的激活，而PIN1过表达则部分逆转了这些效应。在体内，SCO通过调控PIN1/STING/TBK1/IRF3通路显著抑制肿瘤生长。综上所述，这些发现阐明了一种新机制，即SCO通过PIN1/STING/TBK1/IRF3轴抑制胃癌进展，为将SCO开发为胃癌的有前景的治疗候选药物提供了临床前依据。
